 5 weather alerts in effect When are ballots counted in Alaska? 
 Those who voted on Halloween may not have their ballots counted until next week 
 By Hannah Lee Published : Nov. 4, 2026 at 4:28 PM AKST | Updated : 3 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google ANCHORAGE, Alaska (KTUU) - When are the ballots counted in Alaska? It depends on the ballot type and the date you voted, and some ballots will not be counted until next week, according to the Division of Elections. 
 For people who voted on Election Day and had their ballot scanned at a precinct, those results are transmitted to the Director’s Office. If subsequent counts are necessary due to ranked choice voting, those results will be counted at the Director’s Office.
 MORE: Full Alaska election results 
 For people who voted on Election Day at a hand-count precinct, the first-choice vote results are called into the regional elections office Tuesday night, and the tallies are then submitted to the Director’s Office. 
 If subsequent counts are necessary due to ranked choice voting, the Director’s Office will count those results.
 For people who voted on Election Day using a voting tablet, that ballot will be either printed and scanned or printed and called into the regional elections office.
 Regional election offices have already started counting absentee ballots Tuesday night for those received and processed through a certain date. Additional counts will occur this week until all absentee ballots are counted. The last day to receive absentee ballots by mail is Nov. 13 for ballots mailed within the U.S. and its territories, and Nov. 18 for ballots mailed from overseas addresses.
 For those who voted at regional election offices through Oct. 29, ballots were counted on Election Night. Early vote ballots cast between Oct. 30 and Nov. 2 will be counted on Nov. 10, seven days after Election Day.
 The Questioned Board will begin reviewing questioned ballots starting on Thursday, and the ballots won’t be counted until Nov. 10.
 All ballots must be counted no later than Nov. 18, which is 15 days after Election Day. After that final count, the Division of Elections will conduct an additional round of counting the ballots if necessary.
 The target date to certify the election is Nov. 25. The deadline for a recount is on Dec. 5.
